
{{alias}}( order, M, N, A, LDA, R, C, out )
    Computes row and column scale factors intended to equilibrate a matrix `A`
    and reduce its condition number (using the base of the machine as the
    scaling restriction).

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string
        Row-major (C-style) or column-major (Fortran-style) order. Must be
        either 'row-major' or 'column-major'.

    M: integer
        Number of rows in `A`.

    N: integer
        Number of columns in `A`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix `A`.

    LDA: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A` (a.k.a., leading dimension of the
        matrix `A`).

    R: Float64Array
        Output vector for the row scale factors. Should have `M` indexed
        elements.

    C: Float64Array
        Output vector for the column scale factors. Should have `N` indexed
        elements.

    out: Float64Array
        Three element output array whose elements are set to
        `[ ROWCND, COLCND, AMAX ]`.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. The status code indicates the following conditions:

        - if equal to zero, then equilibration was successful.
        - if equal to `i` (a value in the range `[1,M]`), then the row at
        zero-based index `i-1` is exactly zero.
        - if equal to `M+j` (a value in the range `[M+1,M+N]`), then the column
        at zero-based index `j-1` is exactly zero.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var R = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var C = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var out = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > {{alias}}( 'row-major', 2, 2, A, 2, R, C, out )
    0
    > R
    <Float64Array>[ 1.0, 0.25 ]
    > C
    <Float64Array>[ 1.0, 1.0 ]
    > out
    <Float64Array>[ 0.25, 1.0, 4.0 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( M, N, A, sa1, sa2, oa, R, sr, or, C, sc, oc, out, so, oo )
    Computes row and column scale factors intended to equilibrate a matrix `A`
    and reduce its condition number (using the base of the machine as the
    scaling restriction) and using alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing semantics based on starting
    indices.

    Parameters
    ----------
    M: integer
        Number of rows in `A`.

    N: integer
        Number of columns in `A`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix `A`.

    sa1: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A`.

    sa2: integer
        Stride of the second dimension of `A`.

    oa: integer
        Starting index for `A`.

    R: Float64Array
        Output vector for the row scale factors. Should have `M` indexed
        elements.

    sr: integer
        Stride length for `R`.

    or: integer
        Starting index for `R`.

    C: Float64Array
        Output vector for the column scale factors. Should have `N` indexed
        elements.

    sc: integer
        Stride length for `C`.

    oc: integer
        Starting index for `C`.

    out: Float64Array
        Three element output array whose elements are set to
        `[ ROWCND, COLCND, AMAX ]`.

    so: integer
        Stride length for `out`.

    oo: integer
        Starting index for `out`.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var R = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var C = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var out = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 2, 2, A, 2, 1, 0, R, 1, 0, C, 1, 0, out, 1, 0 )
    0
    > R
    <Float64Array>[ 1.0, 0.25 ]
    > C
    <Float64Array>[ 1.0, 1.0 ]
    > out
    <Float64Array>[ 0.25, 1.0, 4.0 ]

    See Also
    --------
